clue.text: Tree climbed next to golf club

indicators.note: next to says the two pieces sit side by side, one after the other

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club used for long shots

explanation.surface: A golfer has scrambled up a tree beside where a club lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewood is a tropical hardwood tree prized for its dark, fragrant timber.

clue.text: Spellbound? That's right and appropriate

explanation.surface: Someone checks that being spellbound is a fitting and correct response.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enthralled and completely absorbed is spellbound, wholly captivated.

clue.text: Part of ancient site bearing weight

parts.note: bearing, as in putting up with, means standing
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A section of an old monument is said to carry a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalith set upright is one element of a prehistoric monument such as Stonehenge.

clue.text: What may be blown from building site, with fellows excited

definitions.text: What may be blown from building site

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Builders, with their excitable mates, send something out across the site at passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: Building workers are stereotyped for whistling at women walking past.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-note admiring whistle is the cliché sound associated with labourers on a construction site.

clue.text: Small operations involving forty-one plants

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: ops is the short form of operations
XLI is forty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Minor surgery is performed on forty-one specimens in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxlips are wild primula flowers, close relatives of the cowslip.

clue.text: Left fool to find lounge

parts.note: an oaf is a clumsy fool

explanation.surface: A clown has been abandoned in a lounge, or so it reads.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs both mean idle about lazily, doing nothing useful.

clue.text: Ancient Dutch legends?

parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney rhyming slang (Dutch plate = mate) for one's wife, so ancient Dutches are elderly spouses, and their legends are their stories

explanation.surface: A question about the folklore of the Netherlands in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' seems to mean from Holland; in London slang 'old Dutch' is a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Superstitious folk beliefs passed down by elderly women, hence any traditional but unfounded notion.

clue.text: Flat key I played to test people's reaction?

indicators.note: played suggests a piece performed in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician tries out a tune in a flat key to see how the audience responds.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to float an idea tentatively to gauge opinion before committing.

clue.text: Gem, ruby initially, set in ring

indicators.note: set in says a letter is placed inside the other piece, as a stone is set in a ring

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of ruby

explanation.surface: A jeweller describes a gemstone, a ruby first, mounted in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrous bead formed in an oyster is valued as a precious stone.

clue.text: But it occurs in February, and not spring?

definitions.text: But it occurs in February, and not spring?

parts.words: But it occurs in February, and not spring?
parts.note: a spring is a leap, yet this day of jumping falls in winter, on 29 February, not in the season of spring

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark that something happens in February rather than spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' reads as the season but also means a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: The extra date, 29 February, added every fourth year to keep the calendar aligned.

clue.text: Very quickly occupying oneself with that large drink?

definitions.meaning: a military phrase for at a running pace, immediately

definitions.text: occupying oneself with that large drink?
definitions.meaning: a double is a double measure of spirits, so someone busy with one is engaged on it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at speed, and literally describes being at work on a double measure of spirits.

clue.text: CID won't park carelessly in N Irish town

indicators.note: carelessly suggests a sloppy job, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Detectives are reluctant to leave their car in a Northern Irish town for fear of bad parking.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in County Down, Northern Ireland, traditionally the burial place of St Patrick.

clue.text: I dance on road in Kingdom

parts.note: the samba is a Brazilian dance

explanation.surface: Someone dances along a road somewhere in the kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kingdom' is not a realm but a name: the engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel, so the answer is the name that comes with Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel's first name stands beside his middle name Kingdom, so each calls up the other.

clue.text: Here players can be sent some notes in binders

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A coach keeps tactics for sending players off in some notes filed in binders.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby and ice hockey, a penalised player is sent to an area off the field for a set time.

clue.text: Temporary ruler, for example, in charge of landlord?

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rent is what a landlord charges a tenant
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Asking whether a stand-in monarch, say, might be put in charge of a landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge of' reads as one phrase meaning managing; it splits into 'in' and 'charge of landlord'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who governs on behalf of a monarch who is too young, ill or absent.

clue.text: County: it provides basic accommodation

parts.note: Beds is the short form of Bedfordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A county is praised for offering simple lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A single rented room serving as both bedroom and living space, a cheap lodging.

clue.text: Lose opportunity, as badly aimed torpedo may?

definitions.meaning: to fail to seize a chance while it is available
a torpedo that is off target fails to hit the ship

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means letting a chance slip, and literally describes a torpedo going wide of its vessel.

clue.text: Young girl forced to speak out

indicators.note: to speak out says the word is said rather than written, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: forced means made, as in made to do something

explanation.surface: A girl is compelled to make her voice heard.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a girl or unmarried young woman, as in maiden.

clue.text: Birds peculiar to caves

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Some birds are found only in caves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar to' reads as 'found only in'; here 'peculiar' is the anagram signal and 'to' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocets are wading birds with long upturned bills, emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: Light timber that's a piece of cake to turn over?

indicators.note: to turn over says the letters are flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a slab is a thick piece, as of cake

explanation.surface: A lightweight wood is said to be easy to flip over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a piece of cake' looks like the idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is an extremely lightweight wood used for model aircraft and rafts.

clue.text: One changing colour, and sounding dreadful

indicators.note: sounding says the word is heard rather than seen, giving a word with the same sound

explanation.surface: Someone whose face is changing colour also sounds awful.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who colours cloth or other materials, giving them a new hue.

clue.text: Des rests, when upset and very anxious

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The setter, Des, takes a break when upset and anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: Des is the setter of this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under strain and worry leaves a person tense and highly agitated.
